title: How much does repeating the oracle actually buy, and what does it cost?
hypothesis: k=3 majority voting removes most of the v8 prompt's run-to-run randomness. The quantity that matters is not the flip RATE but how often a k-majority differs from the verdict an infinitely-repeated oracle would give.
subject: human_thriving v8 prompt, both arms

population.note: Phase A cohort, design-weighted; boundary ~4.4x oversampled

decision_rationale: k=3 adopted. The curve flattens because the residual is rows with no stable oracle answer, which no k removes; k=5 fixes ~33 rows of 6,590.
review: 3 lenses (adversarial, claim-verification, doc-accuracy) + a 4th on the rewrite. Revision 1 had 3 blockers: its headline validation was an algebraic identity (pairwise disagreement is exactly 2/3 x non-unanimity over 3 draws), it compared a production-mix gate figure to a boundary label figure, and its cost multipliers were draw counts. All corrected in revision 2; two further errors found after that.
notes: Estimand is self-consistency, not accuracy: the limit verdict is the oracle's own central tendency, not ground truth. Cost figures were superseded by EXP-004. Inputs staged 2026-08-30 at b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/experiment_inputs/ (phaseA/ and cache_ttl/), verified by sha256; they had been in tmpfs only.

title: Are the reordered prompt's stricter labels better, or merely lower?
hypothesis: Moving the article to the end of the v8 prompt lowers scores (established). This asks whether the rows it drops are junk or true positives, adjudicated against the prompt's own STEP 1 / section 5 rules.
subject: human_thriving v8 prompt-candidate-tail.md vs prompt-candidate.md

population.note: every row whose op-point SIDE differs between arms at k=3

decision_rationale: Evidence favours the reorder (right on 3 of the 4 stable crossings, dropping a 2060 projection, an ODA funding plan and a how-to guidebook) but adoption is an owner ruling and is still open.
review: claim-verification + doc-accuracy. Found the plan's ~860-row figure mis-attributed in BOTH directions across two revisions (production-mix gate vs boundary label).
notes: One stable addition (a harassment settlement) is judged a false positive on ADR-023 reader-risk grounds, not a rule violation; it is arguable both ways. Inputs staged 2026-08-30 at b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/experiment_inputs/ (phaseA/ and cache_ttl/), verified by sha256; they had been in tmpfs only.

title: Does the reordered prompt suppress either protected category?
hypothesis: The section 5b no-regression set exists to stop v8 defining recovery narratives and transitional justice out of the lens. EXP-002 could not test it: those articles are not in the 200-row cohort, so that cohort could not produce the positive. Scored directly under both v8 arms and the v7 prompt, one judge.
subject: the 3 section-5b no-regression articles
decision_rationale: Neither hazard is suppressed; on the transitional-justice row the reordered prompt scores highest of the three prompts tested. The third row fails its assertion under v7 as well, which is a defect in acceptance criterion 2, not in v8.
review: claim-verification; confirmed the quote of the plan's ~860 figure was finally fair.
notes: BLOCKING consequence: acceptance criterion 2 fails today against v7. Owner must drop the Rwanda-EU row or convert its assertion to a delta. Inputs staged 2026-08-30 at b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/experiment_inputs/ (phaseA/ and cache_ttl/), verified by sha256; they had been in tmpfs only.

title: Does the prompt-cache discount survive a corpus-scale run?
hypothesis: Phase A measured repeat passes at a fraction of the first pass and costed k=3 on it. That discount was measured by re-scoring the SAME articles. This tests whether it survives on articles the oracle has never seen, at 30/60/90-minute gaps.
subject: DeepSeek prompt-prefix caching, prompt-candidate-tail.md

population.note: 4 disjoint sets of 50 from the v8 corpus; none ever scored under any v8 prompt

decision_rationale: The prefix cache survives 90 minutes, but the repeat DISCOUNT does not exist for a corpus pass: only the prefix caches, and every article's own tokens are re-paid each pass. k=3 over 6,590 rows is ~$10.32 reordered / ~$54.08 as-is, not the ~$6.92 previously quoted.
review: claim-verification found the FIRST design confounded: its rows came from the Phase A cohort, scored under the same prompt the day before, so its 99.5% hit rate was whole-request reuse. Killed after one pass and redesigned.
notes: Superseded EXP-001's cost table. One prompt, one account, one evening -- DeepSeek publishes no TTL guarantee; 90 minutes is what was tested. Inputs staged 2026-08-30 at b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/experiment_inputs/ (phaseA/ and cache_ttl/), verified by sha256; they had been in tmpfs only.

title: Draw the v8 training corpus to the ruled Gate 0 shape, with a manifest that reconciles
hypothesis: A corpus drawn to the ruled targets (19.5% positive base rate, 63.5/36.5 mix, non-Latin >= 9.76%, class-A >= 0.70%) will correct the v7 corpus's tilt toward easy positives without reshaping the positive class.
subject: the drawable NexusMind archive, 83 cycle files
decision_rationale: Staged on b650-gpu with a manifest recomputed from the written file. All six checks pass, including the two shape clauses that previously had no implementation.
review: 3 lenses. Blockers: the class-A supplement was sampled BELOW the op-point against a verbatim prohibition; clause (c) never executed; the FN cohort was silently deferred. Also a false control claim (the census disagreement was CPython 3.12's change to sum(), not a rounding convention) and a non-census script detector that retracted an owner question.
notes: Known hole, stated not fixed: the class-A instrument matches 0 of 14,660 non-Latin rows, so the class-A target describes the Latin subset only.

title: Find a replacement ADR-015 lens-overlap row for the no-regression set, with a recorded baseline
hypothesis: The Rwanda-EU row failed its own assertion under every prompt including v7 because no observed baseline was ever recorded for it. A replacement drawn from production with its baseline recorded FIRST, and screened against the #107 narrowed Thriving predicate rather than against uplifting v7's scoring behaviour, will hold.
subject: NexusMind data/filtered/ across 5 lenses, stage-2 rows only

population.note: read-only scan on sadalsuud; distinct stage-2 ids per lens, non-stage-2 rows excluded before any score was read because a stage1_low score is an e5 probe estimate, not a model output

decision_rationale: Two rows adopted (one en, one nl) so neither is load-bearing alone. Both verified absent from the drawn corpus and the held-out cohort and present in the drawable pool. The corpus drawer now excludes the no-regression ids by construction, proven on the real pool with two refusal controls at exit 1.
review: The first shortlist was screened on uplifting v7 scores alone and would have adopted a pure-ecology row; #107's narrowed predicate (a process going well FOR PEOPLE, excluding institution-beneficiary) eliminated every one of them. A second candidate with the sharpest money-committed boundary was eliminated on native length: 149 producer chars against 2,033 after enrichment.
notes: The disjointness of the FIRST corpus draw was luck, not enforcement: all three rows then in the set had aged out of the window, so the pool could not contain them - a negative that carried no information. Filed #141 for the non-Latin single-source finding; it is not closable by adding a guard row.

title: Does the CURRENT 4-row no-regression set pass under the adopted v8 prompt?
hypothesis: Acceptance criterion 2 covered 2 of its 4 rows: the two replacements added on 2026-08-30 were selected from uplifting v7 STUDENT scores and had never been scored under any oracle prompt. A student score is not an oracle score -- the Rappler row's stored observed is 6.4864 and it scores 4.900 under the v8 reordered prompt -- so nothing established that the replacements clear the op-point under the prompt Phase B will use.
subject: datasets/adverse/uplifting_no_regression.jsonl (live), 4 rows, full text

population.note: arms A=prompt-candidate-tail.md (adopted), B=prompt-candidate.md, V=filters/uplifting/v7/prompt-compressed.md; one judge across all three; all 4 rows re-scored today rather than stitching the 2 carried-over rows from the 08-29 run

decision_rationale: All four rows PASS under the adopted reordered prompt (analyser exit 0, 4 of 4 covered), so criterion 2 no longer fails before v8 exists and Phase B is unblocked on that count. Two margins sit inside the 0.436/0.687 oracle decoder floor, which is the argument for k=3 stated as data.
notes: commits [] at write time, as for EXP-006 -- the entry is committed with the evidence it cites. A free control fell out of re-scoring the two carried-over rows: a k=3 oracle mean moved by up to 0.484 between 08-29 and 08-31 with judge, prompt hash, text and weights all held fixed, so a <=0.5 movement of a k=3 mean on this population is not an effect.

title: Phase B pre-flight: does the labelling chain survive the labels?
hypothesis: The 6,590-row relabel was declared ready on the strength of the corpus and the prompt. This tests the rest of the chain -- the filter package the labels land in, the k-run aggregation, and the acceptance-gate inputs -- on the grounds that a defect there is only discoverable after the money is spent.
subject: filters/human_thriving/v8, scripts/oracle/average_oracle_runs.py, datasets/adverse/uplifting.jsonl, the staged v8 corpus

population.note: the 8 rows are the FIRST 8 of corpus_v8_final.jsonl, which is grouped by design cell -- they are all class-A, all Latin, all English, not a corpus sample. Billed at PEAK (07:0x UTC Tuesday); off-peak would have been $0.0091.

decision_rationale: Three defects fixed before any bulk spend: the v8 package had no config.yaml so prepare_data wrote 0 examples and exited 0; the k-run aggregator deleted the scope verdicts the runbook requires be reported; and all 18 acceptance-gate rows were 300-char excerpts, now recovered in full from the monthly NexusMind archives. The oracle vendor remains an open owner decision and still gates the run.
notes: The 'windows have rolled -- unrecoverable' premise in #127's thread and the 2026-08-30 rulings is wrong: NexusMind archives monthly (9 tarballs back to 2025-10). The FluxusSource tarballs are NOT a substitute -- they hold producer bytes, 447/133/441 chars for rows whose enriched originals are 14,546/2,917/3,652. Also: the $10.32 k=3 figure is a ceiling, not an estimate -- whole-request cache was observed surviving two days, and whether 6,590 distinct prompts stay cached is a capacity question nobody has measured.

title: Does the ADOPTED (reordered) prompt change which oracle applies STEP 1?
hypothesis: 2026-08-23 decided the Phase B oracle on one row: DeepSeek capped 'Five men arrested for raping a minor' to 3.00 while Gemini rose to 7.43, i.e. Gemini ignored STEP 1. That was measured on the AS-IS prompt. The prompt adopted on 2026-08-30 moves the article to the end, putting STEP 1 much further from the text it judges, and nobody had measured whether adherence changes.
subject: prompt-candidate-tail.md against deepseek-chat and gemini-2.5-flash

population.note: the 9 class-A adverse rows at FULL TEXT (2,107-14,546 chars) for the first time -- every prior class-A number came from 300-char excerpts. spend_usd is the DeepSeek half only; Gemini billed 321,564 input / 8,585 output tokens and the script's cost line applies DeepSeek rates, so no dollar figure is claimed for it.

decision_rationale: The 2026-08-23 argument does not carry to the adopted prompt -- its decisive row is now a tie (1.050 vs 1.025, harm_is_subject 3/3 on both). DeepSeek still leads 8/9 to 7/9 and its one loss is a coin toss both oracles share, while Gemini's extra loss is stable and on the #91 origin row. The measurement is complete; the ruling is the owner's.
notes: Gate B-A passes on NEITHER oracle: both fail 'Parents of baby girl killed at nursery', and on both it is a scope-gate coin toss (DeepSeek 6.10/0.90/6.20, Gemini 7.20/7.15/1.05). --aggregate majority makes it worse on both, removing the one run that got it right. The 5.2x reorder saving is DeepSeek prefix caching and does not transfer: Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns no cache field, so the script's '0.0% cache hit' for it is a construction artifact, not a measurement.

title: Phase B: label the v8 corpus at k=3 with the ruled oracle
hypothesis: The ruled prompt and oracle, applied k=3 over the drawn corpus, produce the training labels for human_thriving v8. Two figures were open going in: the true k=3 cost against a $10.32 ceiling, and the corpus-wide scope-gate flip rate, every prior estimate of which rested on 8-200 rows.
subject: corpus_v8_final (6,590 rows, sha256 5e2cf729), prompt-candidate-tail.md, deepseek-chat

population.note: 4 rows skipped by is_scrape_junk, all JavaScript-required boilerplate at 357-489 chars and all ABOVE the corpus's 300-char floor. spend is priced entirely off-peak; 345 rows of pass 2 ran at peak and bill 2x, so the invoice is about $0.08 higher. One row needed five attempts (reproducible-looking JSON truncation that was in fact stochastic).

decision_rationale: 6,586 labels at k=3, aggregated with every per-run scope verdict retained. H-V8-8's retracted $6.92 was right and its replacement $10.32 was wrong: k=3 re-scores the SAME articles, so passes 2 and 3 hit 99.4% whole-request cache and cost half of pass 1 each.
notes: The 15.35% flip rate must NOT be quoted as label instability: four of the five scope verdicts force all six dimensions to 0-2, so most disagreement is between two out-of-scope categories where the score does not move. The decision-relevant figure is 0.53% -- rows where --aggregate all and --aggregate majority disagree about visibility. Design cells behave as drawn: pos_clear lands at 47.8% (latin) and 48.7% (non-latin) above the op-point, and stage1_low returns 0 of 619 in both scripts.

title: How wide is the v8.1 §2 qualifier fix, and can the leak reach a reader?
hypothesis: The nursery row fails acceptance criterion 1 because §2's qualifier 'especially as a trailing sentence' invites an exception when the post-harm policy change is prominent. Before writing a clause, measure what it would touch -- and whether rows of that shape can cross the op-point at all.
subject: labels_k3.jsonl (6,586 rows, EXP-010), --aggregate all

population.note: labels only; no calls. 4 scrape-junk skips against the 6,590 drawn. Contains 0 adverse and 0 no-regression rows, asserted by the script.

decision_rationale: Clause bounded INSIDE §2, not extended into §1. The §2 scoping touches 67 rows, none above the op-point; the §1-global scoping touches 25 above-op rows including several that read as correct (California wildfire rules 5.43, France social-media ban ruling 4.85, Hong Kong psychiatric facility 4.98). The leak costs criterion 1, not reader trust: no verdict-flipped row in the corpus reaches 4.5 under --aggregate all.
notes: 4.3667 is an EMPIRICAL ceiling, not a mathematical one: one capped run with two at 10.0 gives 7.33 under 'all'. The nursery row's own 4.400 sits above the corpus maximum. The 35-above-under-majority figure independently reproduces the 2026-09-02 label review's count from a separately written instrument. Corrects my own option text, which described the fix as extending §1's money-committed rule.

title: Adjudicate the 47-row class-A supplement, and scan every above-op label for self-contradiction
hypothesis: The supplement carried tp_fp_status: adjudication-pending since the 2026-08-29 draw. Separately: if the oracle names a disqualifier in its own dominant_subject and still scores the row above the op-point, that is a label defect detectable without any lexicon over article text.
subject: the 47 class-A rows in the pos_clear/pos_marginal design cells, and all 456 above-op rows

population.note: the 35 below-op class-A rows are neither TP nor FP under the 2026-08-30 ruling and are not adjudicable

metrics.syria_cluster_corpus_wide: 15 rows, 9 of them above the op-point

decision_rationale: Two thirds of v7's harm-title false positives are demoted at the label level. The 15 survivors are 11 events, so reading them as 15 independent judgements overstates the evidence by ~40%. Six above-op rows name a proposal, plan or 'preparations' in the oracle's own dominant_subject -- a v8.1 candidate DISTINCT from the commencement clause, because §1's announcement rule is written in terms of money and a legislative proposal has no rule pointing at it.
notes: No label was edited. 'harm as the subject' hits are mostly §1's guard working (harm as setting, outcome as occasion) and must not be read as 10 errors. Two owner questions remain open: the Syria cluster under §3, and judicial relief granted to convicted offenders.

title: How much headroom does Phase B2 actually have?
hypothesis: Plan §4b specifies Phase B2 as collecting the student's above-op production positives on class-A shapes. That is the same population the 2026-08-29 corpus draw sampled, so the plan may have been written before the work that discharges it.
subject: b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/pool_v2.jsonl, window filtered_20260815_204839..filtered_20260829_170332

population.note: 83 files; a window is part of a source -- 12 is bounded by the window, not by how many class-A false positives exist

decision_rationale: Phase B2 as written has almost no headroom: the draw took 47 of the 59 available rows and 32 of those already carry labels below the op-point, which is what a hard negative is. The remaining class-A work is label quality inside the corpus, not corpus expansion. The 12 undrawn rows are listed and cost ~$0.02 at k=3, but appending them changes the corpus hash and the manifest.
notes: 17th occurrence of 'establish what a source excludes'. The pool's stored harm_title field is a FALLBACK hand lexicon, recomputed in memory by the draw with the census instrument and never written back; reading it gave 660 where the truth is 59, and neither flag is a superset of the other. I was one step from reporting ~600 rows of headroom.

title: Does the v8.1 prompt fix Gate B-A, and what does each clause cost?
hypothesis: Acceptance criterion 1 fails because the nursery row scores 4.400 against a 3.85 bar. Four v8.1 clauses were written from owner rulings; measure Gate B-A, the no-regression control, and each clause in isolation.
subject: prompt-v8-1.md (32bbbdb68f38), prompt-v8-1b.md (9b71ba58e0c0) and four single-clause ablations against prompt-candidate-tail.md (003cd35a5122)

population.note: balance probed before the first call (7.40 -> 7.23). Run inside the 06:00-10:00 UTC peak window, deliberately. Article text for all 13 rows is already tracked in datasets/adverse.

decision_rationale: ⛔ The premise was wrong: at k=6 under the UNCHANGED v8 prompt the nursery row is 3.608 sd 2.560 -- a PASS. Criterion 1 was never stably failing; 4.400 was a k=3 mean on a 50/50 bimodal row whose standard error at k=3 is 1.48 against a 0.55 margin. v8.1 is therefore a label-quality change, not an unblocking fix -- and more valuable for it, because B_commence removes the coin toss (1.017 sd 0.055). Clauses B, C and D are stable and move nothing else. A is REJECTED as written: the ablation shows it is the sole cause of a regression on the #91 origin row. PART 2: the four clauses are NOT additive -- each individually safe, their union scores the #91 origin row 5.921 with 12/12 in_scope. Leave-one-out isolates a BxD interaction; D held the only sentence that licenses a positive. SHIPPED prompt-v8-4.md = B + C + A3, D dropped, validated at k=12: Gate B-A 9/9, worst class-A sd 2.250 -> 0.205, in_scope runs on class A 3 -> 0, no-regression 4/4. A placebo of +996 chars of section-1 restatement left the origin row at 0.883 sd 0.037, refuting length and location as the cause.
notes: Three errors of mine, all one root: I wrote commencement as a NECESSARY condition when the ruling made it SUFFICIENT; I then declared that fix successful from a k=3 draw that had sampled 3 stable runs out of a 2-in-6 bimodal distribution; and I read 4/4-same-sign drift on the controls as systematic when paired k=6 gives -0.077. On a bimodal row a k=3 mean is a sample of a coin flip. Gate B-A's k must be re-derived before Phase D. The mechanism inside clause A -- probably its 'Lebanon abolishes death penalty' contrast example -- is a hypothesis, not a measurement. Two more of mine: I validated the union by its parts, and I named the contrast example as the cause from reading before the placebo and A3 refuted it. Generalisable: a rule stated as a TEST inside a reasoning step becomes a question asked of every article; the same rule as a CATEGORY in an exclusion list does not.

title: Train human_thriving v8, and find out whether the checkpoint-selection metric was ever live
hypothesis: Phase C step 1: train the student on labels_v84_merged.jsonl. Sub-question that emerged mid-run: --select-metric was accepted but produced no needle metrics, so selection fell back to aggregate MAE. Does correcting it change which epoch ships, and is the resulting checkpoint better?
subject: google/gemma-3-1b-pt + LoRA r=16 alpha=32, 6 epochs, batch 8, lr 2e-5, max_length 512, seed 42. Two arms differing ONLY in checkpoint selection: MAE (pre-fix, epoch 6) vs recall_medium at 4.5 (post-fix, epoch 4).
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.label_provenance: HYBRID: 6130 rows at v8/k=3 (prompt-candidate-tail.md, 003cd35a5122) + 456 above-op rows re-scored at v8.4/k=6 (prompt-v8-4.md, c4705408c477)
population.note: Splits are gitignored (article text at corpus scale, #97). Trained on b650-gpu, CUDA, venv-prodparity.

decision_rationale: The model is trained and the selection defect is fixed, but the two arms are NOT DISTINGUISHABLE and the experiment's headline finding is about the instrument, not the model. Correcting selection DID change the shipped epoch (6 -> 4), refuting the reading -- mine -- that a monotonically falling MAE meant no recall turn had occurred; that inference used MAE to reason about recall, the exact substitution the defect is about. But recall_medium SATURATES at 0.5806 across epochs 4/5/6, so the strict '>' tie-break chose the epoch, not the metric (#144). On the untouched test split epoch 4 leads at 4.5 by two articles on recall and two on specificity, epoch 6 leads on BOTH at 4.25, and they split at 4.0 -- a model that changes rank with a 0.25 threshold move is not distinguishable. Reinforced by seed-42 runs not being bit-reproducible (epoch 6 val MAE 0.5601 vs 0.5605). Epoch 4 kept because it was chosen by a criterion the project endorses, not because it measured better.
review: /review-changes, 4 lenses (reachability, adversarial, claim-verification, doc-accuracy): 4 blockers, 12 warnings, all fixed or filed before the commit was amended.
notes: WEIGHTS ARE NOT ON DISK HERE. adapter_model.safetensors is gitignored and lives only at b650-gpu:~/llm-distillery/filters/human_thriving/v8/model/ (epoch 4) with the MAE-selected arm at model_baseline_mae/ (epoch 6). The committed history/metadata are the provenance; the weights are not reproducible from this repo. The two metadata files use the PRE-AMEND schema (select_metric / select_metric_available / medium_threshold); 1878e7b writes requested_* plus checkpoint-scoped fields, so a future run's file will not match these key-for-key. The checkpoint was produced by the tree that became 1878e7b via an amend, so its exact sha (0697f5a) is dangling; 1878e7b resolves this filter to the same 4.5 and does not change recall_at_k at n=658, so the numbers reproduce, but the artifact was not built by any commit now on a branch. Calibration and the Stage-1 probe are NOT done -- these are raw uncalibrated student outputs and Phase C is incomplete.

title: Phase C part 2 for human_thriving v8: retrain the Stage-1 probe and fit calibration -- do either move recall?
hypothesis: v8 was trained but could not score: no base_scorer, no inference module, no probe, no calibration.json. Raw test recall at 4.5 was 0.514, below all six deployed filters. The plan aims the probe and the calibration at that number. Build both, then measure whether either moves it.
subject: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small + MLPProbe, --objective recall --target-fn 0.02 --seed 42 --device cpu; per-dimension isotonic calibration fitted on the 658-row val split. Student is EXP-015's epoch-4 checkpoint.
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.design_weights: corpus.jsonl inclusion_probability, 0.0341-0.8571 across 17 cells; class-A cells oversampled ~20x. Weighted figures are Horvitz-Thompson estimates for the DRAWABLE population, which EXCLUDES news.google.com (22.1% of production).
population.note: Everything ran on b650-gpu, CPU, venv-prodparity (production pins). CPU chosen so calibration and the mandated Phase D gate device agree; production serves on GPU, so the shipped calibration carries the documented CPU->CUDA 0.1956 term.

decision_rationale: Both artifacts ship and NEITHER MOVED THE TARGET NUMBER. The probe is recall-safe (0 FN at the adopted 1.75 on both splits) so Stage 1 is not what limits recall; the calibration is, measurably, THE SAME RANKER as raw -- Spearman 0.9977, 1.95% discordant pairs, AUC 0.9474 -> 0.9488, and every matched-flag-count recall difference is <=2 articles with inconsistent sign. Its apparent 14-point recall drop at a fixed 4.5 is a THRESHOLD effect: isotonic compresses the top of the scale, so 4.5 calibrated flags 17 rows where 4.5 raw flags 26. The gate's own #95 bands overlap on recall, specificity and F1 -- NOT DISTINGUISHABLE -- so the drop is not reportable as an effect either way. Calibration ships on ADR-008 plus ADR-023's specificity tie-break, explicitly not because it improved anything: on the untouched test split it makes MAE worse in 5 of 6 dimensions (nature_recovery v4's improved test MAE by 22.2%). The threshold 1.75 was chosen against the owner's 2026-08-28 hold-near-pass-through ruling rather than from the script's FN-budget rule, which picked 2.825 and would have cut routing to ~0.52.
notes: THE KEEPER: the Stage-1 threshold belongs to the PROBE, not to the recipe. Seed 7 -- same data, same objective, same code, 0 FN, a BETTER val BCE -- gives a probe on which the configured 1.75 routes 0.7406/0.7567 instead of 0.8876/0.8935, a ~14 pp collapse in Stage-2 routing with every recall number unchanged. Stage 1 is silent by design, so this has no symptom. Guarded: config.yaml records probe_sha256 BESIDE the threshold and inference_hybrid.py refuses to construct on a mismatch; deliberately a different pin from probe/*.pkl.sha256, which travels with the probe and a retrain regenerates. SECOND: hashing is the wrong reproducibility test. Two seed-42 runs are bit-identical in CONTENT (all six tensors np.array_equal, scaler identical) but differ in 134 of 541,144 pickle bytes -- torch storage keys derived from memory addresses -- so sha256sum would have reported 'not reproducible' for a fully reproducible artifact. THIRD: probes shipped before today were UNSEEDED; --seed was added and is now recorded in the pickle's metrics. FOURTH: fit_calibration.py's default edits config.yaml with score_scale_factor = 10/weighted_max; here 1.3787, which with no normalization.json would stretch every score 1.38x. Added --no-config-update, proven by an unchanged config sha256. It is opt-in, so any filter fitted before its normalization still gets the edit. FIFTH, an open gap: the routing asymmetry between Latin and non-Latin is real (6.93 pp, z=2.53) but the FN half is unmeasurable at 8 non-Latin positives -- rule-of-three upper bound 0.375. '0 FN in every script cell' is true and nearly uninformative; the instrument could not have said otherwise. #141 is the blocker. SIXTH, found by the review battery not by me and worth its own line: the routing-gap significance test shipped UNWEIGHTED inside an evidence directory whose thesis is that a sample rate describes no population, because Sigma-w was not recorded per group and so a weighted rate could not be pooled across splits. Recording it (sum_weights*) and redoing the test made the gap LARGER -- 0.0762 weighted against 0.0693 unweighted, z 2.65 vs 2.53 -- so the finding was never at risk and the reporting was. Both SEs are still binomial and therefore optimistic on a stratified design; measured Kish deff 1.068 moves the unweighted z to 2.45. SEVENTH: probe_recall_report.py promised in its own --corpus help text and in the JSON's design_weight_note that weighted columns were 'omitted rather than silently computed with weight 1', and emitted them unconditionally -- the field is there, is populated, and is a different instrument from the one its name claims. EIGHTH: dump_student_scores.py's presence control raised AFTER writing and closing all three output files, so the files it 'refused to emit' were on disk. NINTH: the no-prefilter refusal in base_scorer.py was UNREACHABLE on the hybrid path, because HybridScorer._create_stage2_scorer hardcodes use_prefilter=False -- a documented refusal that could not fire, which is the shape it was written to prevent. TENTH: 'every other inference_hybrid.py hardcodes DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 1.00' was asserted on six surfaces and is true of 2 of 13; worse, the claim's own next clause ('they agree today, so it is harmless') is refuted by nature_recovery v4, which ships config 3.225 against runtime 0.75.

title: Did Phase C work? — and is v8's recall comparable to the fleet's at all?
hypothesis: Phase C was written up as a disappointment: recall 0.486/0.343 against a deployed fleet at 0.59-0.72, with calibration 'not distinguishable'. Both readings depend on comparisons nobody had checked. Test (a) whether v7 and v8 share a positive class at all, and (b) whether the trained student does the thing v8 exists to do -- stop surfacing what v7 wrongly surfaced.
subject: The EXP-016 single forward pass over the 660-row test split (raw and calibrated arms), joined to each row's v7_score from corpus.jsonl. No new inference.
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.note: Every row carries a v7_score; the script refuses to run if any is missing, because a partial join would silently shrink the disputed set. Held-out: the split was untouched by training, checkpoint selection, the probe and the calibration fit.

decision_rationale: Phase C worked, and the metric it was judged on could not show it. (a) THE FLEET COMPARISON IS VOID: v7 and v8 do not share a positive class -- 117 vs 35 positives on the same 660 rows, agreeing on 30, Jaccard 0.246. Recall is conditional on the true class, which is why it survives a change of base RATE and not a change of DEFINITION; 'v8's recall is below all six' compared two different quantities that share a name, and it had been propagated to six surfaces. (b) AGAINST ITS ACTUAL PURPOSE v8 succeeds: of the 87 test rows v7 surfaced that the v8 oracle demotes, the student removes 90.8% raw / 94.3% calibrated, at a cost of keeping only 56.7% / 40.0% of the 30 rows both definitions call positive. (c) THE CONTROL RULES OUT THE TRIVIAL EXPLANATION: AUC on those 117 disputed rows is 0.8454 raw / 0.8521 calibrated against v7's own 0.7218, and at bar 3.0 the student keeps 90% of the good while still removing 62% of the junk -- the two quantities move apart, so it learned a distinction rather than a lower scale. (d) CALIBRATION IS THE BETTER ARM after all, on every axis tied to the filter's purpose; the aggregate-recall band comparison was measuring in the wrong place, and this does not overturn 'not distinguishable' so much as relocate where the difference lives. (e) THE OP-POINT IS A VALUES CALL: under ADR-023 the inherited 4.5 is defensible, because moving to 4.0 buys 5 good articles and readmits 7 junk ones -- the wrong direction when a false positive costs a reader.
notes: CORRECTS EXP-016, which reported the fleet comparison as a finding rather than as an artifact of a changed definition. The corrected surfaces are filters/human_thriving/v8/STATUS.md, that filter's calibration_report.md, docs/evidence/2026-09-04-v8-probe-calibration/README.md, docs/TODO.md, memory/project_session_2026_09_04.md and H-V8-15 in memory/hypothesis-ledger.md. ⚠️ SCOPE: this shows v8 implements the definition the owner chose (#107, the class-A rulings). It does NOT show v8 is better than v7 in any absolute sense -- v7 is judged here against a target it was never trained on, so 0.7218 is a baseline and not a verdict on v7, and whether the new definition is right is an editorial judgement rather than a measurement. ⛔ STILL OPEN: the student under-learns class-A on the highest-scoring v7 rows -- 2 of 6 score ~5 against an oracle ~1, and both are rows v7 scored 6.28 and 6.57, i.e. the ones a reader is most likely to see. n=6; read the direction, not a rate. ⭐ Generalisable: an aggregate metric that POOLS the rows a change exists to demote with the rows it exists to keep cannot show whether the change worked, and will report a real improvement as 'not distinguishable'.
